name: nEXO
summary: nEXO is a proposed large liquid-xenon observatory for xenon-136 neutrinoless double-beta decay. It builds on EXO-200 with a substantially larger isotope inventory and improved background rejection.
detection_principle: A single-phase liquid-xenon time projection chamber measures scintillation and ionization. Three-dimensional position reconstruction, energy resolution and self-shielding distinguish candidate double-beta events from radioactive backgrounds.

status.label: Proposed / near-term construction funding constrained
status.evidence: The full detector has not been built. A May 2025 collaboration presentation reproduces the December 2024 DOE decision to prioritize LEGEND-1000 and notes that near-term US funding is unlikely to permit substantial nEXO advancement, while detector R&D may continue subject to appropriations. DOE reiterated the LEGEND-1000 priority in March 2026.

timeline.event: DOE selected LEGEND-1000 for near-term investment; the decision limited near-term nEXO advancement while allowing continued R&D subject to appropriations.

phases.name: Five-tonne detector proposal
phases.description: The full nEXO detector remains a proposal; the published design sensitivity is not an achieved limit and near-term construction funding is constrained.

phases.name: Detector R&D
phases.description: The collaboration continues development studies; the cited funding decision does not constitute approval or completion of full-detector construction.

results.summary: The report presents the five-tonne detector concept and projected half-life sensitivity; no full-detector measurement is claimed.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
